messages:
Ethan C.: BetaHealth POC hitting 401 + 'scope_mismatch' when calling /v1/chat. They say the key used to work yesterday.
Priya (ae): can you grab their exact curl and response body/headers? quick check: are they switching projects or using a different org?
Customer: here's their command (redacted): `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XYZ\" -d '{"model":"redwood-chat","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"test"}]}'`
Danny (eng): thanks. server 401 + scope_mismatch means token exists but missing `chat:invoke` or `inference:invoke`. Have them call the key inspect endpoint: `GET /v1/keys/inspect` with the same header. That will return owner_org, owner_project, scopes.
Customer: inspect returned `owner_org: beta-health` and `scopes: [\"embeddings:read\"]`
Ethan C.: aha — key is bound to embeddings only. For chat/inference they need `inference:invoke` or `chat:invoke` depending on endpoint.
Marta (security): recommend creating a scoped, short-lived key for the POC with exactly the minimum scopes. Also encourage expiry in 24h/7d. Avoid `*` on prod keys.
Priya (ae): customer worried about accidental charges if they create a new key. billing note: usage is billed to the project that actually makes the call. If they create key in same project, nothing changes; we can add a project spend cap for POC.
OpsBot: To aid debugging, please include the `request-id` from the error response and any `x-rw-` headers. We can trace in logs with request-id.
Danny (eng): sample minimal repro for them after rotating:
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-poc-REPLACE\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
```
Priya (ae): they rotated and tested and still got 401. shared response: `{"error":"unauthorized","request_id":"rq_9a2b3c"}` and header `x-rw-rate-limit: 5000`.
Danny (eng): got it — I'm pulling the trace. OpsBot: start trace for rq_9a2b3c.
OpsBot: Trace started. Found request: key used `owner_org: beta-team` (different from account org). It looks like they copied a key from their staging org.
Customer: oh—we did create multiple orgs. How do we make a key that maps to the POC project?
Ethan C.: Console -> API keys -> Create key -> choose the POC project and add scopes `inference:invoke` (and `chat:stream` if streaming). Also optional IP allowlist.
Marta (security): enable key expiry and IP allowlist. For enterprise POCs, we recommend RBAC: create a service principal on the POC project and issue keys from that principal.
Priya (ae): customer asked if rotating keys will disrupt other integrations.
Danny (eng): rotating a key only affects clients using that exact key. If they replace usage with a new key, no disruption elsewhere.
Customer: rotated and now get 200 OK and model output. Thanks!
Ethan C.: closing loop: I'll send them a short checklist (inspect key, verify scopes, create scoped key under correct project, set expiry/spend cap, include request-id on errors). Thanks team! :tada:
